newsitem.title: USA: Orbital's CEO sees satellite growth.
newsitem.headline: Orbital's CEO sees satellite growth.

text.p: Orbital Sciences Corp's chief executive David Thompson said Monday he expects strong sales from the company's acquisition of employee-owned CTA Inc's satellite manufacturing unit.

"Pulling together CTA's space business with our own is likely to produce accelerated revenue growth," Thompson said in an interview. "I expect $300 million to $500 million in new satellite orders (20 to 30 satellites) as a result of this acquisition in the next two-and-a-half years."
Thompson added the projected orders are in addition to contracts Orbital's and CTA's satellite units would win separately.

Orbital Monday said it bought CTA's satellite and communications business for $12 million in cash and $25 million in assumed debt. CTA's units generated $80 million in revenues in 1996 and have a $150 million order backlog, Orbital said.
"We don't expect to take a charge (to pay for the acquisition)," Thompson said, adding 90 percent of the purchase price was for CTA's satellite unit.
Thompson declined to comment on how the acquisition may affect earnings but said it "would add a couple of pennies a share this year." He added he expected a more significant impact in 1998.
An April 17 First Call consensus estimate of 7 brokers put Orbital's earnings at $0.17 a share in the second quarter and $0.64 a share for the full year.
Thompson said he was not "extremely uncomfortable" with second-quarter projections of $0.17 a share and full-year earnings ranging from $0.65 to $0.67 a share.
Orbital's stock traded at 18-1/8 Monday at noon, up 7/8.
